additional_findings: Placeholder quality is strong: the most copy-paste-dangerous identifiers (CTDC_STUDY_NAME, IDC_COLLECTION_ID, CTDC_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT, image_path, mask_path) all use the non-plausible literal prefix 'REPLACE_ME_' rather than realistic-sounding fake names, which directly reduces the risk of a placeholder being mistaken for (or accidentally used as) a real identifier downstream.

CANCER_TYPE = 'Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma' is a real, plausible CTEP-style disease term (not an obviously fake placeholder string like the others) and is the one value in the config block that could be mistaken for a confirmed/verified term if the inline comment were missed; the comment '# PLACEHOLDER — confirm exact ctep_disease_term value via CTDC skill before querying' is present and adjacent, but it relies on the reader noticing the trailing comment rather than an unmissable token like REPLACE_ME_.

OUTCOME_TIME_COLUMN = 'os_time_days' and OUTCOME_EVENT_COLUMN = 'os_event' are realistic, conventional column names (also flagged inline as PLACEHOLDER) — again plausible-sounding rather than non-plausible, though clearly commented.

Cancer Research 2017) are presented as real/unflagged values, but per notes.md these were copied verbatim from the skill's own SKILL.md rather than invented, so this is appropriate and not a fabrication.

This is a process question rather than a fabrication issue, but worth noting for skill-strictness grading.

No metric values (C-index, AUC, calibration) are fabricated anywhere; Section 9 explicitly instructs 'Do not cite a C-index or AUC value until this cell is run on real data,' which is a strong, well-placed guardrail against the most common failure mode in this kind of eval (presenting plausible-looking fake performance numbers as if real).
